query: Expose order lookup and cancellation to an LLM assistant. Design names, selection descriptions, strict schemas, bounded results, and distinct read versus mutation permissions instead of a generic execute tool.

Our model confuses search_records with get_records and invents record identifiers. Redesign the capabilities and result contracts so discovery and dependent calls have clear preconditions and supported IDs.

A ticket assistant receives a huge raw API payload for each lookup. Specify concise structured output, provenance, pagination, empty and truncated states, and a bounded way to fetch detailed evidence.
Design a reservation tool contract that survives retries and stale inventory. Include idempotency scope, canonical request hashing, state versions, denial errors, and a lost-commit-response exchange.
We have fifty tiny agent tools and an omnibus action tool. Derive a coherent smaller surface from representative user intents while preserving distinct permission and side-effect boundaries.

Give an assistant access to maintenance scheduling without exposing arbitrary HTTP requests. Specify permitted capabilities, model-facing descriptions, trusted identity fields, validation, and cancellation behavior.
Our update tool returns success after accepting a request even when the effect is still pending. Redesign response states and errors so an agent can verify commitment and handle unknown outcomes.

Review units, enums, null versus missing fields, and resource versions in tools for an expense assistant. Produce contracts with examples that make incorrect model arguments detectable before execution.
An LLM needs to search, inspect, and propose edits to a catalogue. Design discoverable read, preview, and commit capabilities with bounded payloads and actionable validation and authorization errors.
Specify an agent tool for bulk document tagging. Keep downstream fan-out and page sizes bounded, distinguish partial results from empty results, and make effects and retry semantics explicit.
Design REST contracts for a calendar API consumed by normal web clients. Define resource names, pagination, consistent errors, versioning, and idempotent updates; no model consumes this interface.

Our model-facing tool contracts are frozen. Evaluate discovery, selection, argument accuracy, dependent-call correctness, and unnecessary requests against realistic tasks before changing any interface.

Implement an MCP server using the existing tool catalogue and schemas. Configure transports, authentication, registration, structuredContent responses, build checks, and Inspector testing without redesigning capabilities.

Define the model output schema for a proposed expense decision with refusal and missing-evidence variants. Focus on generation constraints and semantic validation; no callable tool interface is being added.
Enforce tenant ownership and spending limits immediately before a tool executes. Its public contract already exists; implement the trusted admission function and atomic cumulative budget reservation.

Threat-model a URL-fetching assistant for redirect abuse, internal-network access, leaked credentials, and malicious result text. Verify containment using harmless fixtures rather than redesigning tool descriptions.
A provider committed a booking but our worker crashed before storing its receipt. Design reconciliation, durable checkpoints, retry ceilings, and manual escalation when outcome cannot be determined.
Instrument existing tool calls with logical operation IDs, attempt IDs, safe payload references, normalized action digests, and versioned receipt links. Keep the actual tools and schemas unchanged.
Profile an agent whose tool calls dominate p95 latency. Compare safe read parallelism and result caching under the existing contracts, preserving task quality and tenant-aware invalidation.

Write adapter contract tests for an existing client, checking pagination, timeout classification, and idempotency against a resettable sandbox. We need executable verification of the agreed interface.
